name: Happy Shrimp
tagline: A generative music model that turns a one line prompt into a finished song with lyrics, melody, vocals and arrangement.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The product here is not the web app, it is the model that sings. A coding agent can absolutely build you a prompt box, a job queue, a waveform player and a library view in an afternoon, and none of that matters, because the thing that makes a listenable vocal performance over a coherent arrangement is a large audio model trained on a licensed or at least expensively assembled music corpus. You cannot train that in a session, you cannot train it on a laptop, and the open checkpoints that exist today do not produce singing that survives a second listen. The only honest DIY path is scaffolding: structure, lyrics, chords, MIDI, which is genuinely useful if you write music and completely useless if you wanted a finished track. Treat the glue as free and the voice as the entire bill.
coreLoopDIY: Takes one line of text and emits a song sketch: structure, lyrics, a chord chart and a rendered MIDI backing track, with no vocals and no mix.
requirements: FluidSynth plus a General MIDI soundfont for rendering
An LLM API key in .env for lyrics and chord planning
Basic comfort reading a chord chart, because nothing here sings
whatYouLose: Vocals, which is most of why anyone uses this
A mixed, mastered stereo track instead of a GM soundfont render that sounds like 1998
Genre fidelity: the model knows what a drill hi-hat pattern or a shoegaze guitar tone is, your MIDI does not
Iteration speed, regenerate-until-good is a model feature, not a script feature
Any licensing or clearance story for what comes out the other end
moatNotes: Training audio models is a capital expense with a legal department attached. Both halves are hostile to a weekend build.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the gap between a chord chart and a song with a voice on it is the whole product. Anyone can plan a verse-chorus-verse and pick four chords, that part has been free for centuries. What you are buying is a model that renders timbre, phrasing and a vocal performance that holds together for three minutes, plus the GPU capacity to do it in under a minute and the willingness to own whatever rights questions come with the output. None of those three things get cheaper when you self-host, and the open alternatives are far enough behind that the comparison is not close yet.
notes: The app around the model is a weekend of forms and a player. The moat is the model itself: a trained audio generator, the compute behind it, and someone prepared to answer for the training data.
prompt:
Build a local command line tool called songsketch. Python 3.11, no web UI, no accounts, no telemetry.

What it does: takes one line of text describing a song and produces a song sketch folder on disk. It does NOT generate audio vocals. Be explicit about that in the README.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, typer for the CLI, pydantic for the schema
- An LLM call via the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, key read from OPENAI_API_KEY in .env via python-dotenv
- pretty_midi for MIDI construction
- FluidSynth invoked as a subprocess to render MIDI to WAV using a soundfont path from SOUNDFONT_PATH in .env

Pipeline:
1. `songsketch new "a sad disco song about missing the last train"`
2. One LLM call returns strict JSON validated by pydantic: title, key, tempo_bpm, time_signature, genre_notes, section list (each with name, bars, chord symbols as strings, and lyric lines), and a one paragraph arrangement note describing what each instrument should do.
3. Parse chord symbols into pitch sets locally with a small chord parser you write yourself: triads, sevenths, sus, slash bass. Fail loudly on anything unparseable, do not silently substitute.
4. Build a MIDI file with four tracks: chord pad, bass on roots following the slash bass, a four-on-the-floor-or-genre-appropriate drum pattern chosen from three hardcoded patterns, and a melody track that walks chord tones in the vocal range with one note per lyric syllable (approximate syllables with a simple vowel-group counter, do not pretend it is accurate).
5. Render MIDI to WAV with FluidSynth.
6. Write out: song.json, lyrics.md with section headers, chords.md as a chart, song.mid, song.wav.

In scope: deterministic rerender from song.json via `songsketch render ./out`, and `songsketch regen-lyrics ./out` to redo only the lyrics while keeping structure and chords.

Out of scope, do not build: vocals, singing synthesis, stem separation, mixing, mastering, genre-accurate instrument tones, any cloud storage, any auth.

README must state in the first three lines that this produces a demo-quality sketch for a human to perform or produce, and that it will not sound like a finished record.
